pages.content:
# Module JSON

One file per swerve module (e.g. `frontleft.json`), referenced by name from `swervedrive.json`'s `modules` array. Parsed into `swervelib.core.parser.json.ModuleJson`.

```json
{
  "drive": {
    "type": "sparkmax_neo",
    "id": 1,
    "canbus": ""
  },
  "angle": {
    "type": "sparkmax_neo",
    "id": 2,
    "canbus": ""
  },
  "absoluteEncoder": {
    "type": "revthroughbore_attached",
    "id": 0,
    "channel": 0,
    "canbus": ""
  },
  "inverted": {
    "drive": false,
    "angle": false
  },
  "absoluteEncoderOffset": -45.0,
  "absoluteEncoderInverted": false,
  "location": {
    "front": 12.0,
    "left": 12.0
  }
}
```

| Field                      | Type                                                               | Required             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `drive`                    | [Device](/reference/json-schema/device-types.md#motor-controllers) | yes                  | Drive motor controller. See [Device type strings](/reference/json-schema/device-types.md#motor-controllers).                                                                                                                 |
| `angle`                    | [Device](/reference/json-schema/device-types.md#motor-controllers) | yes                  | Angle/steering/azimuth motor controller.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `absoluteEncoder`          | [Device](/reference/json-schema/device-types.md#absolute-encoders) | yes                  | Module's absolute encoder. See [Device type strings](/reference/json-schema/device-types.md#absolute-encoders).                                                                                                              |
| `gearing`                  | object                                                             | no                   | Per-module override of drive/angle gearing. If omitted, the module uses the defaults from `physicalproperties.json`. Same shape as [physicalproperties.json's `gearing`](/reference/json-schema/physicalproperties-json.md). |
| `inverted.drive`           | boolean                                                            | yes                  | Invert the drive motor.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `inverted.angle`           | boolean                                                            | yes                  | Invert the angle motor.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `absoluteEncoderOffset`    | number (degrees)                                                   | yes                  | Offset so the wheel reads "forward" when physically pointed forward with the bevel gear to the left. Determined by rotating the wheel to face forward and reading the raw absolute encoder value.                            |
| `absoluteEncoderInverted`  | boolean                                                            | no (default `false`) | Invert the absolute encoder's reading.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `absoluteEncoderGearRatio` | number                                                             | no (default `1`)     | Reduction between the absolute encoder and the module's azimuth, as the `X` in `X:1`. Leave it out when the encoder turns 1:1 with the module. Read by the parser but not listed in the JSON Schema file.                    |
| `location.front`           | number (inches)                                                    | yes                  | Distance from the robot's center to the module's center, along the front/back axis.                                                                                                                                          |
| `location.left`            | number (inches)                                                    | yes                  | Distance from the robot's center to the module's center, along the left/right axis.                                                                                                                                          |

## `drive` / `angle` object

| Field    | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`   | string | Controller+motor type string, see [Device type strings](/reference/json-schema/device-types.md#motor-controllers).                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `id`     | number | CAN ID of the motor controller.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `canbus` | string | CAN bus the controller is on: `""` for the SystemCore bus `can_s0`, or the bus number, such as `"1"` for `can_s1`. CTRE controllers also take a CANivore's name; REV and Thrifty controllers only take `""` or a number. See [CAN buses](/reference/json-schema.md#control-system-and-can-buses). |

## `absoluteEncoder` object

| Field     | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`    | string | Encoder type string, see [Device type strings](/reference/json-schema/device-types.md#absolute-encoders).                                                                                                |
| `id`      | number | CAN ID, if the encoder is on CAN. Ignored otherwise.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `channel` | number | SystemCore SmartIO channel, for `_dio` (duty cycle) and `_analog` encoders. Ignored otherwise.                                                                                                           |
| `canbus`  | string | CAN bus, for `_can` encoders: `""` for `can_s0`, or the bus number. A CANcoder also takes a CANivore's name. See [CAN buses](/reference/json-schema.md#control-system-and-can-buses). Ignored otherwise. |

The JSON Schema file requires all four fields (`type`, `id`, `channel`, `canbus`), so set the ones your encoder doesn't use to `0` / `""`.

An `_attached` encoder has no `id`, `channel` or `canbus` of its own: it is read through the module's `angle` motor controller, so it needs a SparkMAX, SparkFlex or Thrifty Nova angle motor. See [Device type strings](/reference/json-schema/device-types.md#absolute-encoders) for which encoders each one accepts.

{% hint style="info" %}
There is no per-module `useCosineCompensator` toggle anymore. Cosine compensation is always applied by the parser. See [Module Behaviors](/explanation/module-behaviors.md) for what it does.
{% endhint %}

# physicalproperties.json

Default gearing and current limits shared by every module, unless a module's own JSON file overrides `gearing`. Parsed into `swervelib.core.parser.json.PhysicalPropertiesJson`.

```json
{
  "gearing": {
    "drive": {
      "gearRatio": 6.75,
      "diameter": 4.0
    },
    "angle": {
      "gearRatio": 12.8
    }
  },
  "statorCurrentLimit": {
    "drive": 40,
    "angle": 20
  }
}
```

| Field                      | Type                | Required          | Description                                          |
| -------------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `gearing.drive.gearRatio`  | number              | yes               | Drive motor reduction, as the `X` in `X:1`.          |
| `gearing.drive.diameter`   | number (inches)     | yes               | Wheel diameter.                                      |
| `gearing.angle.gearRatio`  | number              | yes               | Angle/steering motor reduction, as the `X` in `X:1`. |
| `statorCurrentLimit.drive` | whole number (amps) | no (default `40`) | Drive motor stator current limit.                    |
| `statorCurrentLimit.angle` | whole number (amps) | no (default `20`) | Angle motor stator current limit.                    |

pages.content:
# pidfproperties.json

Default closed-loop PID + feedforward gains shared by every module. Parsed into `swervelib.core.parser.json.PIDFPropertiesJson` (each of `drive`/`angle` is a `swervelib.core.parser.PIDFConfig`).

```json
{
  "drive": {
    "p": 0.5,
    "i": 0.0,
    "d": 0.01
  },
  "angle": {
    "p": 2.0,
    "i": 0.0,
    "d": 0.1
  }
}
```

| Field | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                 |
| ----- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `p`   | number | yes      | Proportional gain.                                                                                                          |
| `i`   | number | yes      | Integral gain.                                                                                                              |
| `d`   | number | yes      | Derivative gain.                                                                                                            |
| `s`   | number | no       | `kS`: static friction feedforward (`SimpleMotorFeedforward`).                                                               |
| `v`   | number | no       | `kV`: velocity feedforward. If left as `0` for the **drive** motor, the parser auto-derives it from the motor's free speed. |
| `a`   | number | no       | `kA`: acceleration feedforward.                                                                                             |

Both `drive` and `angle` are required top-level keys.

## `pidfproperties_sim.json`

Optional. If present, `SwerveParser` uses it instead of `pidfproperties.json` whenever `RobotBase.isSimulation()` is `true`. It has the same shape as above. Use it to tune simulation gains separately from your real robot's gains, without needing to swap files by hand.

{% hint style="warning" %}
There is no more `f` (feedforward) or `iz` (integral zone) field, and no more `output` min/max clamp object. Gains are now expressed as plain PID plus a `SimpleMotorFeedforward`-style `s`/`v`/`a`. See [Schema Changes](/reference/schema-changes.md).
{% endhint %}

See [How to Tune PIDF Gains](/how-to-guides/tune-pidf-gains.md) for a tuning procedure and starting-point values.

pages.content:
# Device Type Strings

Every device `type` string YAGSL's parser recognizes, grouped by device kind. These are the exact enum values enforced by the JSON Schema files in the YAGSL repository (`vendordep/src/test/resources/schemas/`) and resolved in code by `swervelib.core.parser.json.DeviceJson`, `swervelib.core.parser.deserializer.ReflectionsManager` and the per-vendor classes under `swervelib.core.parser.deserializer.reflections`.

{% hint style="info" %}
[config.yagsl.com](https://config.yagsl.com) only lets you pick valid combinations, so you rarely need to type these strings by hand. This page is for reading/debugging existing config files.
{% endhint %}

Type strings are lowercase and are matched exactly. Each vendor's devices are loaded by reflection only when a config uses them, so the matching vendor library has to be installed in your robot project: see [Vendordep Installation](/reference/vendordep-installation.md).

## Gyro

Used in [swervedrive.json](/reference/json-schema/swervedrive-json.md)'s `gyro.type`.

| Type string           | Hardware                                                                                              | Vendor library           |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `pigeon2_can`         | CTRE Pigeon 2.0, over CAN                                                                             | Phoenix 6                |
| `canandgyro_can`      | Redux Canandgyro, over CAN                                                                            | ReduxLib                 |
| `systemcore_internal` | The IMU built into the SystemCore (WPILib `OnboardIMU`), mounted flat. `id` and `canbus` are ignored. | none (part of WPILib)    |
| `navx3_can`           | Studica NavX3, over CAN. **Not available in the 2027 builds yet**, see below.                         | StudicaLib               |
| `custom`              | Any gyro not built by the parser. You supply it yourself.                                             | whatever your gyro needs |

{% hint style="warning" %}
`navx3_can` is still a valid type string, but StudicaLib has no `2027_alpha7` release yet, so the YAGSL 2027 artifacts are built without the NavX3 device class and selecting it fails when the drive is created. Use a [`custom` gyro](/reference/hardware/gyroscopes.md#custom-gyro) until StudicaLib is available.
{% endhint %}

See [Gyroscopes](/reference/hardware/gyroscopes.md) for wiring/calibration notes per device.

## Motor Controllers

Used in [module json](/reference/json-schema/module-json.md)'s `drive.type` and `angle.type`. Format is `<controller>_<motor>`.

| Controller family | Motor suffixes in the schema                          | Vendor library |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `talonfx_`        | `krakenx44`, `krakenx60`, `falcon`, `falcon500`       | Phoenix 6      |
| `talonfxs_`       | `neo`, `neo2`, `neo550`, `vortex`, `pulsar`, `minion` | Phoenix 6      |
| `sparkmax_`       | `neo`, `neo2`, `neo550`, `vortex`, `pulsar`, `minion` | REVLib         |
| `sparkflex_`      | `neo`, `neo2`, `neo550`, `vortex`, `pulsar`, `minion` | REVLib         |
| `nova_`           | `neo`, `neo2`, `neo550`, `vortex`, `pulsar`, `minion` | ThriftyLib     |

e.g. `talonfx_krakenx60`, `sparkmax_neo`, `sparkflex_vortex`, `nova_minion`.

The motor suffix selects the `DCMotor` model used for feedforward and simulation:

| Suffix                | `DCMotor` model                                                           |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `neo`, `neo2`         | `DCMotor.getNEO(1)`                                                       |
| `neo550`              | `DCMotor.getNeo550(1)`                                                    |
| `vortex`              | `DCMotor.getNeoVortex(1)`                                                 |
| `minion`              | `DCMotor.getMinion(1)`                                                    |
| `pulsar`              | ThriftyBot Pulsar (12 V, 3.1 N·m stall, 189 A stall, 7500 RPM free speed) |
| `krakenx44`           | `DCMotor.getKrakenX44(1)`                                                 |
| `krakenx60`           | `DCMotor.getKrakenX60(1)`                                                 |
| `falcon`, `falcon500` | `DCMotor.getFalcon500(1)`                                                 |

Every motor suffix above is a **brushless** motor. SparkMAX itself is still fully supported, but only in brushless mode. There is no `type` value for a brushed motor on any controller family (the old `sparkmax_brushed` and `talonsrx` types are gone). See [Motor Controllers](/reference/hardware/motor-controllers.md) and [Schema Changes](/reference/schema-changes.md).

{% hint style="info" %}
A Thrifty Nova also has to be told which motor is plugged into it. YAGSL sets the Nova's motor type to `MINION` for `nova_minion`, `PULSAR` for `nova_pulsar`, and `NEO` for every other suffix.
{% endhint %}

{% hint style="warning" %}
The schema lists the combinations above, but the parser itself splits the string at the `_` and accepts any controller with any motor suffix (e.g. `talonfx_neo` is not rejected). Not every motor is actually usable on every controller family in practice. Stick to combinations [config.yagsl.com](https://config.yagsl.com) offers, or a combination you've confirmed via the controller's own vendor tooling.
{% endhint %}

See [Motor Controllers](/reference/hardware/motor-controllers.md) for per-controller notes.

## Absolute Encoders

Used in [module json](/reference/json-schema/module-json.md)'s `absoluteEncoder.type`. Format is `<encoder>_<connection>`, where the connection is one of:

* `_can`: its own CAN device, using `id` and `canbus`.
* `_dio`: a duty cycle signal wired to a SystemCore SmartIO port, using `channel`.
* `_analog`: an analog signal wired to a SystemCore SmartIO port, using `channel`.
* `_attached`: wired to the data port of the module's **angle** motor controller and read through that controller. Works with SparkMAX, SparkFlex and Thrifty Nova angle motors.

| Type string                | Hardware                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cancoder_can`             | CTRE CANcoder, over CAN                                                                   |
| `canandmag_can`            | Redux Canandmag, over CAN                                                                 |
| `canandmag_dio`            | Redux Canandmag, wired to a SystemCore SmartIO port                                       |
| `canandmag_attached`       | Redux Canandmag, plugged into the angle motor controller                                  |
| `revthroughbore_dio`       | REV Through Bore Encoder, wired to a SystemCore SmartIO port                              |
| `revthroughbore_attached`  | REV Through Bore Encoder, plugged into the angle motor controller                         |
| `splineencoder_can`        | REV spline encoder, over CAN                                                              |
| `srxmag_analog`            | CTRE Mag Encoder (SRX Mag), wired to a SystemCore SmartIO port                            |
| `srxmag_attached`          | CTRE Mag Encoder (SRX Mag), plugged into the angle motor controller                       |
| `andymarkhexbore_can`      | AndyMark Hex Bore Encoder, over CAN. **Not available in the 2027 builds yet**, see below. |
| `andymarkhexbore_dio`      | AndyMark Hex Bore Encoder, wired to a SystemCore SmartIO port                             |
| `andymarkhexbore_analog`   | AndyMark Hex Bore Encoder, wired to a SystemCore SmartIO port as an analog input          |
| `andymarkhexbore_attached` | AndyMark Hex Bore Encoder, plugged into the angle motor controller                        |
| `thrifty_analog`           | Thrifty absolute encoder, wired to a SystemCore SmartIO port as an analog input           |
| `thrifty_attached`         | Thrifty 10 pin absolute encoder, plugged into a Thrifty Nova angle motor controller       |
| `analog_attached`          | Generic analog encoder (3.3 V on a Spark), plugged into the angle motor controller        |
| `analog5v_attached`        | Generic 5 V analog encoder, plugged into a SparkMAX/SparkFlex angle motor controller      |
| `dutycycle_attached`       | Generic duty-cycle encoder, plugged into the angle motor controller                       |

Which `_attached` types work depends on the angle motor controller:

| Angle motor controller | `_attached` types it accepts                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SparkMAX / SparkFlex   | `revthroughbore`, `canandmag`, `srxmag`, `andymarkhexbore` and `dutycycle` (all read as a duty cycle encoder), `analog` (3.3 V), `analog5v` (5 V). Not `thrifty_attached`. |
| Thrifty Nova           | `thrifty`, `revthroughbore`, `canandmag`, `srxmag`, `andymarkhexbore`, `dutycycle`, `analog`. Not `analog5v_attached`.                                                     |
| TalonFX / TalonFXS     | None. Use a `_can`, `_dio` or `_analog` encoder.                                                                                                                           |

{% hint style="warning" %}
`andymarkhexbore_can` is still a valid type string, but AndyMark's library has no `2027_alpha7` release yet, so the YAGSL 2027 artifacts are built without its device class and selecting it fails when the drive is created. Wire the encoder to a SmartIO port (`andymarkhexbore_dio` / `andymarkhexbore_analog`) or to the angle motor controller (`andymarkhexbore_attached`) instead.
{% endhint %}

See [Absolute Encoders](/reference/hardware/absolute-encoders.md) for per-device notes and calibration tips.

pages.title: Motor Controllers
pages.content:
# Motor Controllers

Supported motor controller/motor combinations for module drive and angle motors

{% hint style="danger" %}
**TalonSRX and brushed SparkMAX are no longer supported.** The pre-2026.8.05 `talonsrx` and `sparkmax_brushed` types have been removed. YAGSL now only drives brushless motors through YAMS's `SmartMotorController` abstraction. See [Schema Changes](/reference/schema-changes.md).
{% endhint %}

## Motor Checklist

* [ ] All motors spin counterclockwise positive (CCW+); document any inversions required to achieve that.
* [ ] Motor is updated to the latest firmware.
* [ ] Motor has a unique CAN ID that matches its module JSON.
* [ ] Wheels are aligned forwards with all bevels facing the same way before first enable.
* [ ] PID is tuned. See [Tune PIDF Gains](/how-to-guides/tune-pidf-gains.md).

## Configuring a motor

Each module JSON (`frontleft.json`, etc.) has a `drive` and an `angle` motor, both `DeviceJson` objects of the form `"<controller>_<motor>"`:

```json
{
  "drive": { "type": "sparkflex_vortex", "id": 5, "canbus": "" },
  "angle":  { "type": "sparkmax_neo550", "id": 6, "canbus": "" }
}
```

The `<motor>` suffix tells YAGSL which `DCMotor` model to use for feedforward and simulation characterization (free speed, stall torque, etc.). It must match the physical motor attached to that controller.

`canbus` is the CAN bus the controller is on: `""` for the SystemCore bus `can_s0`, or the bus number, such as `"1"` for `can_s1`. See [Control system and CAN buses](/reference/json-schema.md#control-system-and-can-buses).

## Supported controller × motor combinations

| Controller                                | `type` values                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [TalonFX](#talonfx-kraken-x60-kraken-x44) | `talonfx_krakenx44`, `talonfx_krakenx60`, `talonfx_falcon`, `talonfx_falcon500`                                   |
| [TalonFXS](#talonfxs)                     | `talonfxs_neo`, `talonfxs_neo2`, `talonfxs_neo550`, `talonfxs_vortex`, `talonfxs_pulsar`, `talonfxs_minion`       |
| [SparkMAX](#sparkmax)                     | `sparkmax_neo`, `sparkmax_neo2`, `sparkmax_neo550`, `sparkmax_vortex`, `sparkmax_pulsar`, `sparkmax_minion`       |
| [SparkFlex](#sparkflex)                   | `sparkflex_neo`, `sparkflex_neo2`, `sparkflex_neo550`, `sparkflex_vortex`, `sparkflex_pulsar`, `sparkflex_minion` |
| [Nova (ThriftyBot)](#thrifty-nova)        | `nova_neo`, `nova_neo2`, `nova_neo550`, `nova_vortex`, `nova_pulsar`, `nova_minion`                               |

{% hint style="warning" %}
This is the full list the JSON schema accepts for feedforward/simulation purposes. It is **not** a claim that every combination is physically wireable. Respect real hardware constraints: a TalonFX is built into Kraken X44/X60 and Falcon 500 motors, and the other controllers only drive motors their connectors and firmware support. Pick the row for your actual controller, and the `<motor>` suffix that matches what's physically bolted to it.
{% endhint %}

Each controller family needs its vendor library installed in your robot project (Phoenix 6 for `talonfx_*`/`talonfxs_*`, REVLib for `sparkmax_*`/`sparkflex_*`, ThriftyLib for `nova_*`). YAGSL loads it by reflection only when your config uses that controller. See [Vendordep Installation](/reference/vendordep-installation.md).

Every controller takes a bus number in `canbus`. Only CTRE controllers (`talonfx_*`, `talonfxs_*`) also take a name, for a CANivore. REV and Thrifty controllers reject anything other than `""` or a bus number.

{% hint style="warning" %}
**CTRE default bus changed in 2027.** A TalonFX or TalonFXS with `"canbus": ""` is now on `can_s0`, like every other vendor's devices. It used to end up on `can_s2`; if yours are wired to `can_s2`, set `"canbus": "2"`.
{% endhint %}

## TalonFX (Kraken X60 / Kraken X44)

TalonFX is the controller for Kraken X44/X60 and (legacy) Falcon 500 motors. Commonly used as a drive motor for its power and efficiency versus REV NEOs.

* [Kraken product page](https://wcproducts.com/products/kraken)
* Upgradeable/configurable via [Tuner X](https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/tuner/index.html). Watch the LED status code when debugging. Settings changed in Tuner X are overwritten on startup by YAGSL.

{% hint style="warning" %}
If running Falcon 500 v2 (effectively discontinued), apply the [Loctite fix](https://content.vexrobotics.com/vexpro/Falcon/217-6515-753-Falcon500-V2-Upgrade.pdf).
{% endhint %}

## TalonFXS

TalonFXS is CTRE's controller for third-party/non-Kraken brushless motors (NEO, NEO Vortex, Minion, Pulsar) wired through CTRE's ecosystem, with the same Tuner X tooling and CAN/CANivore support as TalonFX.

## SparkMAX

REV SparkMAX, brushless mode (NEO / NEO 550 / NEO Vortex / Minion / Pulsar via the appropriate `<motor>` suffix).

* [Product page](https://www.revrobotics.com/rev-11-2158/)
* Requires the [REV Hardware Client](https://docs.revrobotics.com/rev-hardware-client/gs/install) to test PID, run at a set percentage, and update firmware.

{% hint style="warning" %}
The SparkMAX must be disconnected from the CAN bus **on startup** to be recognized by the REV Hardware Client.
{% endhint %}

To tune PID directly on the controller: open REV Hardware Client → select the SparkMAX → Telemetry tab → set to position control while adjusting gains in the left pane.

**Checklist**

* [ ] Unique CAN ID.
* [ ] Latest firmware.
* [ ] Rotates CCW+ (invert programmatically if not).
* [ ] PID tuned for one drive motor and one angle motor before wiring the rest.

## SparkFlex

REV SparkFlex, brushless mode (same motor suffixes as SparkMAX, primarily used with NEO Vortex).

* [Product page](https://www.revrobotics.com/next-generation-spark-neo/)
* Same [REV Hardware Client](https://docs.revrobotics.com/rev-hardware-client-2) workflow and startup-disconnect caveat as SparkMAX.

Both Spark controllers can read an absolute encoder plugged into their data port (the `_attached` encoder types): see [Absolute Encoders](/reference/hardware/absolute-encoders.md#attached-encoders). `canbus` must be `""` or a bus number; port names such as `"can_s1"` are no longer accepted.

## Thrifty Nova

ThriftyBot Nova, supported again in 2027 through YAMS's `NovaWrapper`. Requires the **ThriftyLib** vendordep.

* `type` is `nova_<motor>`. YAGSL configures the Nova's own motor type from the suffix: `MINION` for `nova_minion`, `PULSAR` for `nova_pulsar`, and `NEO` for every other suffix.
* `canbus` must be `""` (for `can_s0`) or a bus number. Anything else is rejected with an error that lists the bus numbers.
* A Nova angle motor can read an absolute encoder plugged into its data port, including the Thrifty 10 pin encoder (`thrifty_attached`). It does not support `analog5v_attached`. See [Absolute Encoders](/reference/hardware/absolute-encoders.md#attached-encoders).

**Checklist**

* [ ] Unique CAN ID.
* [ ] Latest firmware.
* [ ] Rotates CCW+ (invert programmatically if not).
* [ ] ThriftyLib vendordep installed.

***

### General motor tips (apply regardless of controller)

* Confirm CCW+ rotation on the bench before mounting. See [When to Invert](/how-to-guides/determine-inversion.md).
* Tune one drive motor and one angle motor fully before copying gains to the other three modules; see [Tune PIDF Gains](/how-to-guides/tune-pidf-gains.md).
* Current limits and gearing live in `physicalproperties.json` (or a per-module `gearing` override). See [physicalproperties.json Reference](/reference/json-schema/physicalproperties-json.md).

# Absolute Encoders

Supported absolute encoder types for a module's absoluteEncoder field

YAGSL supports most common FRC absolute encoders. An absolute encoder is required for every module. It's what lets the angle motor know its true position on power-up, without needing to "home" against a hard stop.

The live reading shows up on the dashboard under `Mechanisms/swerve/modules/<name>/encoder` (degrees). Use it to find the value for `absoluteEncoderOffset` in each module's JSON. See [Telemetry, Simulation & Vision](/explanation/telemetry-and-vision.md) for the full NT tree.

## Absolute Encoder Checklist

* [ ] All absolute encoders read counterclockwise positive (CCW+).
* [ ] Magnetic absolute encoders get a good read on the magnet both at rest and while the robot is moving (check for wiggle/wire strain).
* [ ] Each encoder has a unique CAN ID or SmartIO channel.
* [ ] Encoder reads the full `0°`–`360°` range.

## Configuring an absolute encoder

`absoluteEncoder` is a `DeviceJson`-shaped object, `"<encoder>_<connection>"`:

```json
{
  "absoluteEncoder": { "type": "cancoder_can", "id": 11, "channel": 0, "canbus": "" },
  "absoluteEncoderOffset": -18.281,
  "absoluteEncoderInverted": false
}
```

* `absoluteEncoderOffset`: degrees to add so the wheel reads `0°` when facing forward with the bevel gear to the left. Read this off `Raw Absolute Encoder` on the dashboard with the wheel manually squared up, then enter the negative of that raw value (config.yagsl.com does this arithmetic for you).
* `absoluteEncoderInverted`: should rarely, if ever, need to be `true`.
* For `_can` encoders, set `id` and `canbus`. `canbus` is `""` for the SystemCore bus `can_s0`, or the bus number, such as `"1"` for `can_s1`; a CANcoder also takes a CANivore's name. See [Control system and CAN buses](/reference/json-schema.md#control-system-and-can-buses).
* For encoders wired to a SystemCore SmartIO port (`_dio` and `_analog`), set `channel` to the SmartIO channel instead of `id`/`canbus`.
* For `_attached` encoders, `id`, `channel` and `canbus` are all unused: the encoder is read through the module's angle motor controller.

{% hint style="warning" %}
If a module spins continuously without settling, try inverting its angle motor before suspecting the absolute encoder.
{% endhint %}

## Supported absolute encoder types

| Device                                                                                                      | `type`                     | Connection                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [REV Throughbore](https://www.revrobotics.com/rev-11-1271/)                                                 | `revthroughbore_attached`  | Plugged into the angle motor controller's duty-cycle port                         |
| REV Throughbore                                                                                             | `revthroughbore_dio`       | SystemCore SmartIO (duty cycle)                                                   |
| CTRE [CANcoder](https://pro.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/hardware-reference/cancoder/index.html) | `cancoder_can`             | CAN; bus number or CANivore name. Requires Phoenix 6.                             |
| [Canandmag](https://docs.reduxrobotics.com/canandmag/getting-started)                                       | `canandmag_attached`       | Plugged into the angle motor controller's duty-cycle port                         |
| Canandmag                                                                                                   | `canandmag_dio`            | SystemCore SmartIO (duty cycle)                                                   |
| Canandmag                                                                                                   | `canandmag_can`            | CAN; bus number or ReduxLib bus string. Requires ReduxLib.                        |
| [SRX Mag Encoder](https://store.ctr-electronics.com/srx-mag-encoder/)                                       | `srxmag_attached`          | Plugged into the angle motor controller's duty-cycle port                         |
| SRX Mag Encoder                                                                                             | `srxmag_analog`            | SystemCore SmartIO (analog input)                                                 |
| [AndyMark Hex Bore](https://www.andymark.com/)                                                              | `andymarkhexbore_attached` | Plugged into the angle motor controller's duty-cycle port                         |
| AndyMark Hex Bore                                                                                           | `andymarkhexbore_dio`      | SystemCore SmartIO (duty cycle)                                                   |
| AndyMark Hex Bore                                                                                           | `andymarkhexbore_analog`   | SystemCore SmartIO (analog input)                                                 |
| AndyMark Hex Bore                                                                                           | `andymarkhexbore_can`      | CAN. *Not available in the 2027 builds yet, see below.*                           |
| Spline Encoder                                                                                              | `splineencoder_can`        | CAN (REV); bus number only. Requires REVLib.                                      |
| Thrifty absolute encoder                                                                                    | `thrifty_attached`         | Plugged into a Thrifty Nova angle motor controller's data port (10 pin encoder)   |
| Thrifty absolute encoder                                                                                    | `thrifty_analog`           | SystemCore SmartIO (analog input)                                                 |
| Generic analog (5V)                                                                                         | `analog5v_attached`        | Plugged into a SparkMAX/SparkFlex angle motor controller's analog port, 5 V range |
| Generic analog                                                                                              | `analog_attached`          | Plugged into the angle motor controller's analog port (3.3 V range on a Spark)    |
| Generic duty-cycle                                                                                          | `dutycycle_attached`       | Plugged into the angle motor controller's duty-cycle port                         |

{% hint style="warning" %}
`andymarkhexbore_can` is still accepted by the schema, but AndyMark's library has no `2027_alpha7` release yet, so the YAGSL 2027 artifacts are built without its device class and creating the drive with it fails. Use `andymarkhexbore_dio`, `andymarkhexbore_analog` or `andymarkhexbore_attached` for now.
{% endhint %}

### Attached encoders

The `_attached` connection means the encoder is wired directly into the module's **angle** motor controller rather than a SmartIO port or the CAN bus. YAGSL reads it back through that controller's vendor API. This replaces the old `SwerveDrive.pushOffsetsToEncoders()` mechanism from pre-2026.8.05 releases.

Which `_attached` types work depends on the angle motor controller:

| Angle motor controller | Accepted `_attached` encoders                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SparkMAX / SparkFlex   | `revthroughbore`, `canandmag`, `srxmag`, `andymarkhexbore` and `dutycycle` (all read from the duty-cycle absolute encoder input), `analog` (3.3 V) and `analog5v` (5 V) from the analog input. Not `thrifty_attached`. |
| Thrifty Nova           | `thrifty`, `revthroughbore`, `canandmag`, `srxmag`, `andymarkhexbore`, `dutycycle` and `analog`. The Nova is told which encoder is on its data port from the type string. Not `analog5v_attached`.                     |
| TalonFX / TalonFXS     | None. Use a `_can`, `_dio` or `_analog` encoder instead.                                                                                                                                                               |

***

### General absolute encoder tips (apply regardless of device)

* Set the offset with the wheel physically squared to the robot, not by eyeballing degrees on the dashboard from an arbitrary position.
* Re-check offsets any time a module is disassembled. Even a "put it back the same way" rebuild can shift the magnet by a few degrees, and swerve is unforgiving of small offset errors at low speed.
* If you swap a module between corners, its encoder wiring moves with it. The offset value does not automatically follow. See [Verify Module Locations](/how-to-guides/verify-module-locations.md).

pages.content:
# Standard Conversion Factors

Known-good gearing values for common commercial-off-the-shelf swerve modules

These are known-good `gearRatio`/`diameter` values for common COTS swerve modules. Set them either as the drivetrain-wide default in `modules/physicalproperties.json`, or as a per-module override in a module's own `gearing` field (module-level `gearing` wins if both are present):

```json
"gearing": {
  "drive": { "gearRatio": 6.75, "diameter": 4 },
  "angle": { "gearRatio": 12.8 }
}
```

* `drive.gearRatio`: motor revolutions per wheel revolution, as `X` where the ratio is `X:1`.
* `drive.diameter`: wheel diameter in **inches**.
* `angle.gearRatio`: motor revolutions per full azimuth revolution, as `X:1`.

The config generator at [config.yagsl.com](https://config.yagsl.com) has these built in as presets. You generally won't need to type these by hand, but they're listed here for reference and for teams hand-editing JSON.

## MAX Swerve

| Pinion | `angle.gearRatio` | `drive.gearRatio` | `drive.diameter` |
| ------ | ----------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| 12T    | 46.42             | 5.50              | 3                |
| 13T    | 46.42             | 5.08              | 3                |
| 14T    | 46.42             | 4.71              | 3                |

## Swerve Drive Specialties (SDS)

| Module  | `angle.gearRatio` | `drive.gearRatio` | `drive.diameter` |
| ------- | ----------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| MK4 L1  | 12.8              | 8.14              | 4                |
| MK4 L2  | 12.8              | 6.75              | 4                |
| MK4 L3  | 12.8              | 6.12              | 4                |
| MK4 L4  | 12.8              | 5.14              | 4                |
| MK4i L1 | 21.4285714286     | 8.14              | 4                |
| MK4i L2 | 21.4285714286     | 6.75              | 4                |
| MK4i L3 | 21.4285714286     | 6.12              | 4                |
| MK5i R1 | 26                | 7.03              | 4                |
| MK5i R2 | 26                | 6.03              | 4                |
| MK5i R3 | 26                | 5.27              | 4                |
| MK4n L1 | 18.75             | 7.13              | 4                |
| MK4n L2 | 18.75             | 5.9               | 4                |
| MK4n L3 | 18.75             | 5.36              | 4                |
| MK5n R1 | 26.09             | 7.03              | 4                |
| MK5n R2 | 26.09             | 6.03              | 4                |
| MK5n R3 | 26.09             | 5.27              | 4                |

## Thrifty Swerve

Steering gear ratio is **25:1** for both configurations below (12T pinion, 3" wheel, NEO-driven). Check the gear-ratio chart on your Thrifty Swerve for other pinion/output combinations.

| Output gear | `angle.gearRatio` | `drive.gearRatio` | `drive.diameter` |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| 18T         | 25                | 15                | 3                |
| 16T         | 25                | 16.9              | 3                |

## Plummer Industries

| Configuration      | `angle.gearRatio` | `drive.gearRatio` | `drive.diameter` |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| Corner, Mid Ratio  | 28                | 4                 | 2.5              |
| Corner, High Ratio | 28                | 3.25              | 2.5              |

## Deriving your own

If your module isn't listed, compute the reduction from the module's datasheet: `gearRatio` is motor revolutions per output revolution (drive → wheel, angle → azimuth), and `diameter` is the wheel diameter in inches, measured on a slightly-worn tread (a fresh, un-worn wheel measures larger than it will after a few matches, and using the worn number keeps odometry accurate longer). Overestimating `diameter` makes the robot think it's traveled less than it has, so odometry-driven autonomous routines undershoot; verify against a real drive-straight test as described in [Verify Module Locations](/how-to-guides/verify-module-locations.md).

pages.content:
# Vendordep Installation

Vendor dependencies YAGSL requires and how to install them

YAGSL 2027 targets WPILib `2027_alpha7` (Java 25) on the SystemCore. It is published as **two** vendordeps, one per WPILib command framework. Install exactly one of them: each one declares a conflict with the other.

| Command framework | Vendordep name        | Vendordep URL                                       |
| ----------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Commands v2       | `YAGSL (Commands v2)` | `https://cdn.yassrobotics.com/yagsl_commands2.json` |
| Commands v3       | `YAGSL (Commands v3)` | `https://cdn.yassrobotics.com/yagsl_commands3.json` |

{% hint style="warning" %}
The old `https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/yagsl.json` URL (and the `.../YAGSL/yagsl/yagsl.json` one before it) is the 2026 vendordep. Do not use it for a 2027 project; remove `vendordeps/yagsl.json` if you are upgrading.
{% endhint %}

## Install YAGSL

### Online

In VS Code, run **WPILib: Manage Vendor Libraries → Install new libraries (online)** and paste the URL for your command framework:

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="Commands v2" %}

```
https://cdn.yassrobotics.com/yagsl_commands2.json
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Commands v3" %}

```
https://cdn.yassrobotics.com/yagsl_commands3.json
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

To pin a project to one release, use the versioned URL instead, for example `https://cdn.yassrobotics.com/yagsl_commands2-2026.10.09.json`.

See the [WPILib guide to installing 3rd-party libraries](https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/vscode-overview/3rd-party-libraries.html#installing-libraries) for the general workflow.

### Offline

Every [GitHub release](https://github.com/Yet-Another-Software-Suite/YAGSL/releases) has a `<version>-YAGSL-Offline.zip` asset (for example `2026.10.09-YAGSL-Offline.zip`). It contains a `maven` folder and a `vendordeps` folder that merge into your WPILib `2027_alpha7` home folder, which the WPILib installer creates:

| OS            | Extract into                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Windows       | `C:\Users\Public\wpilib\2027_alpha7` |
| macOS / Linux | `~/wpilib/2027_alpha7`               |

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="Windows (PowerShell)" %}

```powershell
Expand-Archive -Path "$HOME\Downloads\2026.10.09-YAGSL-Offline.zip" -DestinationPath "C:\Users\Public\wpilib\2027_alpha7" -Force
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="macOS / Linux" %}

```bash
unzip -o ~/Downloads/2026.10.09-YAGSL-Offline.zip -d ~/wpilib/2027_alpha7
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

Afterwards you should have `wpilib/2027_alpha7/maven/swervelib/...` and `wpilib/2027_alpha7/vendordeps/yagsl_commands2.json` / `yagsl_commands3.json`. Then run **WPILib: Manage Vendor Libraries → Install new libraries (offline)** and pick **YAGSL (Commands v2)** or **YAGSL (Commands v3)**.

{% hint style="info" %}
The offline zip only contains YAGSL. YAMS and any vendor libraries you need have to be installed offline separately.
{% endhint %}

## What gets installed

Both vendordeps resolve from the Maven repository at `https://cdn.yassrobotics.com/`, group `swervelib`:

| Vendordep              | Java artifacts                   | Packages                                   |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `yagsl_commands2.json` | `YAGSL-core` + `YAGSL-commands2` | `swervelib.core.*` + `swervelib.commands2` |
| `yagsl_commands3.json` | `YAGSL-core` + `YAGSL-commands3` | `swervelib.core.*` + `swervelib.commands3` |

These replace the single `YAGSL-java` artifact of the 2026 releases.

## Required vendor libraries

The only library YAGSL's vendordep requires is the matching **YAMS** vendordep. WPILib offers to install it when it's missing.

| YAGSL vendordep        | Requires                                           | YAMS in turn requires                                                    |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `yagsl_commands2.json` | `https://cdn.yassrobotics.com/yams_commands2.json` | WPILib Commands v2 (`CommandsV2.json`, from the WPILib vendor libraries) |
| `yagsl_commands3.json` | `https://cdn.yassrobotics.com/yams_commands3.json` | WPILib Commands v3 (`CommandsV3.json`, from the WPILib vendor libraries) |

## Optional vendor libraries

Hardware vendor libraries are **not** required by the vendordep anymore. YAGSL loads a vendor's device classes by reflection only when your JSON config uses one of that vendor's devices, so you install the libraries for the hardware you actually have:

| Vendor library | Install it if your config uses                                                                           |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| REVLib         | `sparkmax_*`, `sparkflex_*`, `splineencoder_can`, or an `_attached` encoder on a Spark                   |
| CTRE Phoenix 6 | `talonfx_*`, `talonfxs_*`, `pigeon2_can`, `cancoder_can`                                                 |
| ReduxLib       | `canandgyro_can`, `canandmag_can`                                                                        |
| ThriftyLib     | `nova_*`, or an `_attached` encoder on a Nova                                                            |
| *(none)*       | `systemcore_internal` (WPILib's built in `OnboardIMU`), and `_dio` / `_analog` encoders on SmartIO ports |

Phoenix 5 is no longer needed for anything.

{% hint style="danger" %}
If a config uses a device whose vendor library is missing, the project still builds, but robot code crashes with a missing class error when `SwerveParser.createSwerveDrive(...)` creates that device. Install the vendor library and redeploy.
{% endhint %}

{% hint style="warning" %}
**NavX3-CAN (`navx3_can`) and the AndyMark CAN Hex Bore encoder (`andymarkhexbore_can`) are not available in the 2027 builds yet.** StudicaLib and AndyMark's library have no `2027_alpha7` release, so YAGSL 2027 is built without their device classes. See [Gyroscopes](/reference/hardware/gyroscopes.md#navx3-can) and [Absolute Encoders](/reference/hardware/absolute-encoders.md) for what to use instead.
{% endhint %}

Use the 2027 (`2027_alpha7`) release of each vendor library, installed from the vendor's own vendordep URL or the WPILib Vendor Dependencies panel. See the [WPILib guide to installing 3rd-party libraries](https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/vscode-overview/3rd-party-libraries.html#installing-libraries).

You'll also want the vendor's own tuning/firmware tools installed on your development machine (not a robot-code dependency, but needed to configure/calibrate hardware):

* [REV Hardware Client 2](https://docs.revrobotics.com/rev-hardware-client-2)
* [CTRE Tuner X](https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/installation/installation-frc.html)
* Studica Hardware Manager (NavX3-CAN)

pages.content:
# API Reference

YAGSL's own Java surface is intentionally small: `SwerveParser` reads your [JSON config](/reference/json-schema.md) and hands you back a fully-built **YAMS** `SwerveDrive`. From that point on, you're driving and configuring a YAMS object, not a YAGSL-specific one, so the authoritative API reference lives in the YAMS docs, not here.

## YAGSL packages

YAGSL 2027 is split into a command framework agnostic core and one small package per WPILib command framework. Which packages you have depends on the [vendordep you installed](/reference/vendordep-installation.md).

| Package                                                   | Artifact          | What's in it                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `swervelib.commands2`                                     | `YAGSL-commands2` | `SwerveParser` for Commands v2. Returns a `yams.commands2.swerve.SwerveDrive` bound to your `Subsystem`.                                |
| `swervelib.commands3`                                     | `YAGSL-commands3` | `SwerveParser` for Commands v3. Returns a `yams.commands3.swerve.SwerveDrive` bound to your `Mechanism`.                                |
| `swervelib.core.parser`                                   | `YAGSL-core`      | The base `SwerveParser` (JSON reading, the `SwerveDriveDevices` / `SwerveModuleDevices` records), `CANBuses`, `PIDFConfig`.             |
| `swervelib.core.parser.json` (and `.json.modules`)        | `YAGSL-core`      | The classes each JSON file is read into: `SwerveDriveJson`, `ModuleJson`, `DeviceJson`, `PhysicalPropertiesJson`, `PIDFPropertiesJson`. |
| `swervelib.core.parser.deserializer` (and `.reflections`) | `YAGSL-core`      | `ReflectionsManager` and the per-vendor device classes, loaded by reflection.                                                           |
| `swervelib.core.telemetry`                                | `YAGSL-core`      | `SwerveDriveTelemetry`.                                                                                                                 |

The pre-2027 `swervelib.parser.*` and `swervelib.telemetry.*` packages are now `swervelib.core.parser.*` and `swervelib.core.telemetry.*`. Robot code should import `SwerveParser` from `swervelib.commands2` or `swervelib.commands3`, not from `swervelib.core.parser`.

## SwerveParser entry points

Every method is `static`. Parse the directory first, then create the drive:

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="Commands v2" %}

```java
import swervelib.commands2.SwerveParser;
import yams.commands2.config.SwerveDriveConfig;
import yams.commands2.swerve.SwerveDrive;

var cfg = new SwerveDriveConfig().withSubsystem(this);

SwerveParser.parse(new File(Filesystem.getDeployDirectory(), "swerve/base"));
SwerveDrive drive = SwerveParser.createSwerveDrive(cfg);
```

{% endtab %}

{% tab title="Commands v3" %}

```java
import swervelib.commands3.SwerveParser;
import yams.commands3.config.SwerveDriveConfig;
import yams.commands3.swerve.SwerveDrive;

var cfg = new SwerveDriveConfig().withMechanism(this);

SwerveParser.parse(new File(Filesystem.getDeployDirectory(), "swerve/base"));
SwerveDrive drive = SwerveParser.createSwerveDrive(cfg);
```

{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}

| Method                                                            | Defined in                                                              | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SwerveParser.parse(File directory)`                              | `swervelib.core.parser.SwerveParser`                                    | Reads the JSON directory into the static `swerveDriveJson`, `pidfPropertiesJson`, `physicalPropertiesJson` and `moduleJsons` fields. Throws `UncheckedIOException` if a file can't be read.          |
| `SwerveParser.parseDirectory(File directory)`                     | `swervelib.core.parser.SwerveParser`                                    | Same, but throws the checked `IOException`.                                                                                                                                                          |
| `SwerveParser.readJson(File file, Class<T> type)`                 | `swervelib.core.parser.SwerveParser`                                    | Reads one JSON file into one of the `swervelib.core.parser.json` classes.                                                                                                                            |
| `SwerveParser.createSwerveDrive(SwerveDriveConfig config)`        | `swervelib.commands2.SwerveParser` / `swervelib.commands3.SwerveParser` | Builds the modules and gyro from the parsed JSON, applies them to your `SwerveDriveConfig`, and returns the framework's `SwerveDrive`.                                                               |
| `SwerveParser.createSwerveDriveDevices(SwerveDriveConfig config)` | `swervelib.commands2.SwerveParser` / `swervelib.commands3.SwerveParser` | Same, but returns a `SwerveDriveDevices<SwerveDrive>` record: `swerveDrive()`, `gyro()` and `modules()` (one `SwerveModuleDevices` per module, with `drive()`, `azimuth()` and `absoluteEncoder()`). |

{% hint style="warning" %}
`parse(...)` returns a core `swervelib.core.parser.SwerveParser`, which has no `createSwerveDrive`. The 2026 style chain `SwerveParser.parse(dir).createSwerveDrive(cfg)` and the older `new SwerveParser(dir).createSwerveDrive(cfg)` no longer compile. Call the two static methods one after the other, as shown above.
{% endhint %}

`SwerveParser.createSwerveDriveDevices(config)` is the one place YAGSL hands back something other than YAMS objects: alongside the `SwerveDrive`, it returns the raw vendor motor controller/encoder/ gyro objects it built, for the rare case where you need to call a vendor-specific method `SmartMotorController` doesn't expose. `gyro()` is `null` for a `custom` gyro. See [How to access raw hardware devices](/how-to-guides/access-raw-hardware-devices.md).

## YAMS classes you get back

| Class                                                         | Commands v2                                      | Commands v3                               | YAMS API reference                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SwerveDrive`                                                 | `yams.commands2.swerve.SwerveDrive`              | `yams.commands3.swerve.SwerveDrive`       | [SwerveDrive](https://yagsl.gitbook.io/yams/api-reference/java-reference/swerve/swerve-drive)                |
| `SwerveDriveConfig`                                           | `yams.commands2.config.SwerveDriveConfig`        | `yams.commands3.config.SwerveDriveConfig` | [SwerveDriveConfig](https://yagsl.gitbook.io/yams/api-reference/java-reference/swerve/swerve-drive-config)   |
| `SwerveInputStream`                                           | `yams.commands2.swerve.SwerveInputStream`        | `yams.commands3.swerve.SwerveInputStream` | [SwerveInputStream](https://yagsl.gitbook.io/yams/api-reference/java-reference/swerve/swerve-input-stream)   |
| `SwerveModule` (per-module)                                   | `yams.core.mechanisms.swerve.SwerveModule`       | same                                      | [SwerveModule](https://yagsl.gitbook.io/yams/api-reference/java-reference/swerve/swerve-module)              |
| `SwerveModuleConfig` (built internally from your module JSON) | `yams.core.mechanisms.config.SwerveModuleConfig` | same                                      | [SwerveModuleConfig](https://yagsl.gitbook.io/yams/api-reference/java-reference/swerve/swerve-module-config) |

The framework specific `SwerveDrive` and `SwerveDriveConfig` extend the shared `yams.core.mechanisms.swerve.SwerveDrive` and `yams.core.mechanisms.config.SwerveDriveConfig`, which is where most of their methods are documented.

The full YAMS API reference (all mechanisms, motor controllers, units, and math helpers, not just swerve) is at [yagsl.gitbook.io/yams](https://yagsl.gitbook.io/yams/api-reference/java-reference).

## Javadoc

| Library                              | Javadoc                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| YAGSL                                | [yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/javadocs](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/javadocs/)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `swervelib.commands2.SwerveParser`   | [SwerveParser (Commands v2)](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/javadocs/swervelib/commands2/SwerveParser.html)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `swervelib.commands3.SwerveParser`   | [SwerveParser (Commands v3)](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/javadocs/swervelib/commands3/SwerveParser.html)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `swervelib.core.parser.SwerveParser` | [SwerveParser (core)](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/javadocs/swervelib/core/parser/SwerveParser.html)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `swervelib.core.parser.CANBuses`     | [CANBuses](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/javadocs/swervelib/core/parser/CANBuses.html)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `swervelib.core.parser.json`         | [JSON classes](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/javadocs/swervelib/core/parser/json/package-summary.html)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| YAMS                                 | [yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAMS/javadocs](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAMS/javadocs/)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| YAMS `SwerveDrive`                   | [Commands v2](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAMS/javadocs/yams/commands2/swerve/SwerveDrive.html), [Commands v3](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAMS/javadocs/yams/commands3/swerve/SwerveDrive.html), [core](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAMS/javadocs/yams/core/mechanisms/swerve/SwerveDrive.html)                   |
| YAMS `SwerveDriveConfig`             | [Commands v2](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAMS/javadocs/yams/commands2/config/SwerveDriveConfig.html), [Commands v3](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAMS/javadocs/yams/commands3/config/SwerveDriveConfig.html), [core](https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAMS/javadocs/yams/core/mechanisms/config/SwerveDriveConfig.html) |

{% hint style="info" %}
Only `SwerveParser` and the JSON-file classes under `swervelib.core.parser.json` are YAGSL-specific. If you find yourself calling a method on `SwerveDrive`, `SwerveModule`, `SwerveDriveConfig`, `SwerveModuleConfig`, or `SwerveInputStream`, you're looking at YAMS API. Go to the links above, not the YAGSL source, for the authoritative docs and Javadoc.
{% endhint %}

## Where to look for what

* **"What JSON fields exist?"** → [JSON Schema Reference](/reference/json-schema.md) (this site).
